claims.assertion: The GPS track shows the driver drove 14.5 km against an optimal 8.6 km, i.e. +5.9 km (+69%), so the trip was not made by the shortest and most direct route.
One off-route segment ran 12:12–12:22, covering 6.47 km where the optimal route covers 1.32 km, adding 5.15 km, and it was never exempted by any ground in the policy.

No traffic incident near the route was recorded during the trip window (weather fair, no rain), so the driver's claim that his GPS 'rerouted' him has no supporting traffic fact; the recorded congestion on Ayer Rajah Expressway (band 4, 30–39 km/h) and Jurong Town Hall Road (band 5, 40–49 km/h) is neither an incident nor the band 1–2 severe congestion the policy accepts as corroboration.
The chat contains only pickup coordination messages and no proposal of a route change by the driver before the deviation, so there was no mutual agreement preceding the off-route segment.

This is a metered RydeTAXI trip charged $31.56 including distance fare $20.43 for 14.5 km and time fare $5.76 for 22.2 min, so the added off-route distance directly entered the fare at the per-km rate of $1.41/km ($20.43 ÷ 14.5 km).
The refundable amount is the unexempted segment's extra distance times the per-km rate: 5.15 km × $1.41/km = $7.26, rounded to the cent.
No waiting fee was charged ($0.00) and surge was 1.0×, so the only disputed item is the distance overcharge; no ride-hailing surcharge inflates the figure.
The driver's 90-day record shows 2 upheld route disputes including this one, meeting the repeated-route-violation profile, so an account-review flag should be attached to the award.

weaknesses: The policy's data layer only keeps off-route segments above 0.2 km, but the segment start/end is a map-matching estimate: the $7.26 figure rests on F3's 5.15 km, which the driver could argue is inflated by matching error, and the small residual between F1's +5.9 km and F3's 5.15 km (0.75 km) is expressly not refundable under RD-2.

The driver's account in F9 ('I followed my GPS; it rerouted me') is a claim of reasonable cause; although F12 shows no incident and F10/F11 show only moderate bands (30–49 km/h), those speed-band records are the evidence the other side will use to argue the reroute was traffic-driven, and F11 (Jurong Town Hall Road, band 5) is not obviously far from the route.

There is a 12-minute, 1194 m gap between the deviation and the optimal route (F3) which could also be read as a passenger-requested stop; the rider's silence in chat (F7, F8 contain only pickup messages) cuts both ways, since an unrecorded verbal stop request cannot be disproved.
F14 shows the rider had 1 dispute in the last 90 days (0 upheld), which the driver may use to suggest a pattern of fare complaints.

claims.assertion: The GPS record shows one continuous off-route stretch from 12:12 to 12:22 in which 6.47 km was driven where the optimal route covers 1.32 km, adding 5.15 km — this is the whole of the excess distance on the trip.

Because this is a RydeTAXI metered trip, the refund is confined to the unexempted segment's extra kilometres at the trip's per-km rate, i.e. 5.15 km × $1.41 = $7.26, and not the rider's claimed 'extra distance' of the full 5.9 km gap.

The rider never named an alternative place to go and the driver's statement is that the routing came from the app's GPS reroute, so no segment qualifies for the passenger-requested-stop exemption under RD-3(a).

Waiver under RD-4(a) is unavailable: traffic records show no incident anywhere near the optimal route during the trip window (F12), so the reroute cannot be excused as caused by a road closure, accident or breakdown.

Waiver under RD-4(b) also fails: the two speed-band records are band 4 (30–39 km/h) on the Ayer Rajah Expressway and band 5 (40–49 km/h) on Jurong Town Hall Road, neither of which reaches the band 1–2 severe-congestion definition, and a band reading is at most corroborative in any event.

There is no chat record of the driver proposing a route change and the rider agreeing before 12:12; the only pre-trip messages are pickup-location pleasantries at 12:03, so the RD-5 consent exemption does not apply to the 12:12–12:22 segment.
No waiting charge was levied on this trip ($0.00) and no other unpublished add-on appears in the breakdown, so no FARE-1 exposure arises and the only contested amount is the metered distance.

The driver's 90-day history shows 2 prior upheld route disputes, so if this case is found against him RD-6 makes the matter 'repeated' and an account-review flag is added — the profile alone does not establish this trip's deviation.

weaknesses: The GPS is against us on the merits: F3 records a single 5.15 km detour reaching 1194 m from the optimal route, and F1/F2 confirm +5.9 km and +8.4 min, which is far beyond match noise, so the client cannot defeat RD-1 liability.

The client's own statement (F9 'I followed my GPS; it rerouted me') is the weakest possible basis — it is a statement that is contradicted in effect by the system records F10–F12, and under the system-record-wins rule it cannot carry RD-4.

The client's 90-day profile (F15, 2 upheld route disputes, 1093 trips) is exactly the trigger the other side will use for RD-6, so pressing an untenable full denial of any deviation risks both the $7.26 refund finding and the account flag.

The rider's claim of '14 km, refund the extra distance' would over-refund under RD-2: the formula uses only the unexempted segment's 5.15 km at $1.41/km, so conceding the segment costs the client $7.26, not the $8.35 that F4 shows was billed on the 5.9 km gap.

The fact table records a single off-route segment on this RydeTAXI trip: 12:12–12:22, 6.47 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.32 km, adding 5.15 km and reaching 1194 m from the optimal route [F3], against an optimal route of 8.6 km versus 14.5 km actually driven [F1]. Under RD-1 no percentage or absolute threshold applies, so this unexplained deviation breaches the driver's shortest-and-most-direct-route obligation [F1][F3][RD-1]. The driver's statement that "my GPS rerouted me" [F9] is a statement, and it is contradicted by the system records; it therefore cannot carry a reasonable-cause exemption under RD-4 [F9][F12][RD-4].

No exemption applies to that segment. No traffic incident was recorded near the route during the trip window [F12], and the only speed-band records are band 4 (30–39 km/h) on Ayer Rajah Expressway [F10] and band 5 (40–49 km/h) on Jurong Town Hall Road [F11] — neither reaching the band 1–2 severe-congestion definition, and band evidence is at most corroborative when an incident exists [F10][F11][F12][RD-4]. Nothing in the chat shows the driver naming a route change and the rider agreeing before the 12:12 segment start; the only pre-departure messages are 12:03 pickup coordination [F7][F8], so RD-5 does not exempt the segment [F7][F8][F3][RD-5]. No rider-named stop exists, so RD-3 gives no relief either [F3][F7][F9][RD-3].

This is a metered RydeTAXI trip, so the refund is confined to the unexempted segment's extra kilometres at the trip's own per-km rate, not the full 5.9 km gap [F6][F1][RD-2]. The rate derives from the fare breakdown: $20.43 distance fare ÷ 14.5 km = $1.41/km [F6][F4]. The refund is therefore 5.15 km × $1.41/km = $7.26 [F3][F6][RD-2]. The 0.75 km residual between F1's +5.9 km and F3's 5.15 km is matching residual and is not refundable under RD-2 [F1][F3][RD-2]. No waiting fee was charged and surge was 1.0×, so there is no FARE-1 add-on in dispute beyond the metered distance [F6][F5][FARE-1].

Because RD-2 yields a refund above zero, the case is established against the driver, and the profile shows route_disputes_upheld_90d = 2 [F15], making this a repeated breach; under RD-6 the award carries an account-review flag, with the profile used only as the basis for that additional action and not to decide the deviation itself [F15][F3][RD-6].

events.body:
RIDER: We reviewed your trip and found one part of the route was not justified. The records show a detour of about 5 km off the shortest route, with no traffic incident or severe congestion recorded at the time, so we're refunding the extra distance.

We're issuing you a $7.26 Ryde voucher. It'll be added to your Ryde account — no action needed on your part.

Thanks for flagging this and for riding with Ryde.

— Ryde Support

DRIVER: We reviewed this trip and found part of the route you drove was not the shortest and most direct one, and we couldn't verify a reason for the detour from the trip records. Because of that, we've issued the rider a $7.26 Ryde voucher covering the extra distance.

Your profile also shows similar route issues upheld recently, so your account is being sent for review. A reviewer will look at your recent route records and any explanations you've provided.

This notice is about the account review only. You don't need to do anything right now.

— Ryde Support

actions.detail: account action is never automatic; queued for Ryde review

what_would_change: Had an LTA incident been recorded on the stretch F3 replaced, before it started, RD-4 would exempt it (−$7.26).

claims.assertion: The GPS track shows the driver drove 14.5 km against an optimal 8.6 km, i.e. +5.9 km (+69%), so the trip was not made by the shortest and most direct route.
One off-route segment ran 12:12–12:22, covering 6.47 km where the optimal route covers 1.32 km, adding 5.15 km, and it was never exempted by any ground in the policy.

No traffic incident near the route was recorded during the trip window (weather fair, no rain), so the driver's claim that his GPS 'rerouted' him has no supporting traffic fact; the recorded congestion on Ayer Rajah Expressway (band 4, 30–39 km/h) and Jurong Town Hall Road (band 5, 40–49 km/h) is neither an incident nor the band 1–2 severe congestion the policy accepts as corroboration.
The chat contains only pickup coordination messages and no proposal of a route change by the driver before the deviation, so there was no mutual agreement preceding the off-route segment.

This is a metered RydeTAXI trip charged $31.56 including distance fare $20.43 for 14.5 km and time fare $5.76 for 22.2 min, so the added off-route distance directly entered the fare at the per-km rate of $1.41/km ($20.43 ÷ 14.5 km).
The refundable amount is the unexempted segment's extra distance times the per-km rate: 5.15 km × $1.41/km = $7.26, rounded to the cent.
No waiting fee was charged ($0.00) and surge was 1.0×, so the only disputed item is the distance overcharge; no ride-hailing surcharge inflates the figure.
The driver's 90-day record shows 2 upheld route disputes including this one, meeting the repeated-route-violation profile, so an account-review flag should be attached to the award.

weaknesses: The policy's data layer only keeps off-route segments above 0.2 km, but the segment start/end is a map-matching estimate: the $7.26 figure rests on F3's 5.15 km, which the driver could argue is inflated by matching error, and the small residual between F1's +5.9 km and F3's 5.15 km (0.75 km) is expressly not refundable under RD-2.

The driver's account in F9 ('I followed my GPS; it rerouted me') is a claim of reasonable cause; although F12 shows no incident and F10/F11 show only moderate bands (30–49 km/h), those speed-band records are the evidence the other side will use to argue the reroute was traffic-driven, and F11 (Jurong Town Hall Road, band 5) is not obviously far from the route.

There is a 12-minute, 1194 m gap between the deviation and the optimal route (F3) which could also be read as a passenger-requested stop; the rider's silence in chat (F7, F8 contain only pickup messages) cuts both ways, since an unrecorded verbal stop request cannot be disproved.
F14 shows the rider had 1 dispute in the last 90 days (0 upheld), which the driver may use to suggest a pattern of fare complaints.

claims.assertion: The GPS record shows one continuous off-route stretch from 12:12 to 12:22 in which 6.47 km was driven where the optimal route covers 1.32 km, adding 5.15 km — this is the whole of the excess distance on the trip.

Because this is a RydeTAXI metered trip, the refund is confined to the unexempted segment's extra kilometres at the trip's per-km rate, i.e. 5.15 km × $1.41 = $7.26, and not the rider's claimed 'extra distance' of the full 5.9 km gap.

The rider never named an alternative place to go and the driver's statement is that the routing came from the app's GPS reroute, so no segment qualifies for the passenger-requested-stop exemption under RD-3(a).

Waiver under RD-4(a) is unavailable: traffic records show no incident anywhere near the optimal route during the trip window (F12), so the reroute cannot be excused as caused by a road closure, accident or breakdown.

Waiver under RD-4(b) also fails: the two speed-band records are band 4 (30–39 km/h) on the Ayer Rajah Expressway and band 5 (40–49 km/h) on Jurong Town Hall Road, neither of which reaches the band 1–2 severe-congestion definition, and a band reading is at most corroborative in any event.

There is no chat record of the driver proposing a route change and the rider agreeing before 12:12; the only pre-trip messages are pickup-location pleasantries at 12:03, so the RD-5 consent exemption does not apply to the 12:12–12:22 segment.
No waiting charge was levied on this trip ($0.00) and no other unpublished add-on appears in the breakdown, so no FARE-1 exposure arises and the only contested amount is the metered distance.

The driver's 90-day history shows 2 prior upheld route disputes, so if this case is found against him RD-6 makes the matter 'repeated' and an account-review flag is added — the profile alone does not establish this trip's deviation.

weaknesses: The GPS is against us on the merits: F3 records a single 5.15 km detour reaching 1194 m from the optimal route, and F1/F2 confirm +5.9 km and +8.4 min, which is far beyond match noise, so the client cannot defeat RD-1 liability.

The client's own statement (F9 'I followed my GPS; it rerouted me') is the weakest possible basis — it is a statement that is contradicted in effect by the system records F10–F12, and under the system-record-wins rule it cannot carry RD-4.

The client's 90-day profile (F15, 2 upheld route disputes, 1093 trips) is exactly the trigger the other side will use for RD-6, so pressing an untenable full denial of any deviation risks both the $7.26 refund finding and the account flag.

The rider's claim of '14 km, refund the extra distance' would over-refund under RD-2: the formula uses only the unexempted segment's 5.15 km at $1.41/km, so conceding the segment costs the client $7.26, not the $8.35 that F4 shows was billed on the 5.9 km gap.

points.response: Conceded as to the arithmetic of the detour, but the driver's framing omits that F3 shows the detour reached 1194 m from the optimal route over ten minutes with no incident or severe congestion recorded (F12, F10, F11), which is not explainable GPS drift.

Agreed on the RD-2 measure: the rider's demand is confined to the unexempted segment, 5.15 km (F3) at the trip's own per-km rate of $1.41 derived from $20.43 ÷ 14.5 km (F4, F6), i.e. $7.26, and not the $8.35 billed on the 5.9 km gap.

The driver's concession that no passenger-named place exists defeats RD-3(a) against himself: under RD-3(b) a stop the driver chose himself, creating an off-route segment without telling the rider beforehand, is not exempt, and F7/F8 show no such request in the chat.

Agreed and adopted: F12 records no incident near the optimal route during the trip window and weather was fair with 0.0 mm rain (F13), so the driver's 'my GPS rerouted me' statement (F9) cannot be a reasonable cause under RD-4(a) and loses to the system records.
Agreed: bands 4 and 5 (30–49 km/h) in F10 and F11 do not reach the band 1–2 definition and are at most corroborative, so RD-4(b) yields no exemption for the 12:12–12:22 segment.
Agreed: the only messages before the deviation are 12:03 pickup coordination (F7, F8), so no consent message precedes the 12:12 segment start (F3) and RD-5 cannot exempt it.

Agreed that no waiting fee or unpublished add-on was levied ($0.00 waiting, platform $1.47, surge 1.0×), so FARE-1 adds nothing beyond confirming the meter charged $20.43 for the 14.5 km actually driven (F6, F1).

Agreed on the mechanics and the limit of the profile: F15's 2 upheld route disputes plus this one make the breach 'repeated' for the RD-6 account-review flag, but F15 alone cannot decide the deviation — F3 does that.

Conceded on liability as to the deviation itself: F1 (+5.9 km on an 8.6 km optimal route) and F3 (5.15 km added on the 12:12–12:22 segment) are system records and cannot be argued away, so the obligation in RD-1 was breached on that segment.

The 12:12–12:22 stretch is the only off-route segment in the fact table, and nothing in RD-3, RD-4 or RD-5 exempts it, so it stands as an unexempted segment under RD-1 and is the sole basis for any refund under RD-2.

The rider's reading of the traffic facts is the one the driver himself must live with — F12 records no incident near the route and F10/F11 are only bands 4 and 5 (30–49 km/h), below the band 1–2 severe congestion the policy requires — but note that F9 is the driver's statement and, per the system-record-wins rule, adds nothing either way to RD-4.
Agreed that no pre-deviation agreement exists: F7 and F8 are 12:03 pickup messages with no route proposal before the 12:12 segment start, so RD-5 does not exempt the segment.

The metered structure is correctly stated (F6 shows distance $20.43 for 14.5 km, i.e. $1.41/km, plus time $5.76), and it is exactly this structure that makes only the unexempted segment's kilometres recoverable, not the 5.9 km gap the rider pleads in F1.
The arithmetic is conceded: F3's 5.15 km extra at the F6-derived rate of $1.41/km gives $7.26, and RD-2 allows nothing for the 0.75 km residual between F1 and F3.
Accepted — F6 shows waiting $0.00 and F5 shows surge 1.0x, so there is no FARE-1 add-on in dispute and the case turns only on RD-2 distance.

F15's 2 upheld route disputes in 90 days against 1093 completed trips is thin evidence of repetition, and RD-6 requires a finding against the driver in this case before any flag; the profile is an add-on only and must not decide the case, so the flag should at most follow the $7.26 finding and not aggravate it.

notices.text:
